open_points.subject: randomly minted record identifiers
open_points.text: `trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again.
open_points.question: Which module owns random identifier generation and the atomic collision check for each of these records?
options: Each domain module mints its own identifiers and asks `store` to reject collisions
`store` mints every random identifier inside the record-writing transaction
One shared lower-level identifier capability owns generation while `store` checks uniqueness
open_points.default_guess: Have `store` mint the identifier inside the transaction that creates the record.

open_points.subject: operation-node input contract violation
open_points.text: `NodeExecution` M23 is written by `effects` for the record that concludes an operation element ... and by `runs` for every other record; a receiving node concluded [for target-port validation failure] did not run.
open_points.question: Who writes the `contract_violation` NodeExecution when an operation node's incoming value fails validation before the operation is reached?
options: `runs` writes it because `runs` owns edge delivery and target-port validation
`runs` detects the violation but calls `effects` to write it because it concludes an operation element
`effects` owns both validation and the record for operation inputs
open_points.default_guess: Let `runs` write it because no operation attempt or effect transaction exists.

open_points.subject: agent-name uniqueness
open_points.text: names are unique in an installation, and a configuration repeating one is refused at start
open_points.question: Which module owns and performs the start-time uniqueness check for agent names?
options: `installation.load_installation` validates names with the rest of the configuration
`surface` validates names when constructing its authentication table
A separate configuration validation capability performs the check

open_points.subject: pinned release dependencies and sandbox runtime
open_points.text: The pinned Python dependencies and sandbox runtime of A20 rule 3 are a release artifact built and checked outside the running kernel; at run time only `sandbox.probe_sandbox` checks that a sandbox works.
open_points.question: What component owns the authoritative dependency/runtime version pins and verifies that the built release matches them?
options: `data_provider` owns the version-pin data and the release build consumes it
`sandbox` owns the runtime pins while the package lockfile owns kernel dependencies
A named release-build artifact outside the runtime modules owns and verifies all pins
open_points.default_guess: Use one named release lock/build artifact outside the runtime modules as the authoritative owner, with `sandbox.probe_sandbox` limited to runtime operability.
